This is the fourth game in the XX89 series by Phr00t starting with 3079. This is an improvement on 3079 and 3089 that does the series justice. It keeps some of the good things that were in 4089 but get's rid of most of the bad from that game. 

Comparing to 3079 this game has better graphics, better weapons, better controls, and is overall way more polished. It doesn't have the character that the first game had. The first game I have lots of nostalgia for which means it is higher up than this game on my list even if this game is a better game. Compared to the two the game developer came a long way with his skills and knowledge of game design.

Comparing to 3089 this game is the more refined older brother of the two. The gameplay is very similar but there are more mechanics in this game that makes it a lot less rinse and repeat than 3089. It's a refreshing take between the two and I would recommend this one over 3089 and 3079 (even though I love 3079 more). 

I had a good time playing this game until the final bit. I was somehow able to select multiple endings which then gave me some weird prompts that didn't make sense and then I was locked out of being able to see what happened. I tied to back my save up before getting to this point but didn't do it correctly because the same file isn't inside the normal game files. If you want to play this game I would strongly suggest taking your time with the endings and back up your save before the ending under "C:\users\*your user*\5089" so you don't make the same mistake as me and have to try to figure out how to restart the game but not loose all of your progress (I was able to get my character's stats into a new save).

I enjoyed this game quite and bit and most of the bugs I ran into has an easy solution. I love 3079 better than this game because that was the first game in the series and it has the nostalgia factor but this game is the best out of the series so far.

I actually love this overlooked gem of a game. Sure, you can just grab the five nearest guns and start blasting, but once you take the time to study the weapon components, options, and utilities in depth, the game's possibilities just keep opening in myriad layers, which make it the best kind of RPG. Even before I have completed a first run with my blunt-force, knuckle-dragging, armed-to-the-teeth Schwartzenegger-core style, ideas for my more sophisticated, James Bond style stealthy, aircraft pilot, tech-savvy character come to mind. Either that or I go full Highlander and melee berserk on my enemies.
The only criticism of this game is, that even if you love the 90's nostalgic look and feel of the game, Phroot, God bless his heart, and eyes, has a questionable grasp of aesthetics, so many may find the game hard to look at.

While this game has an interesting concept, I think its been executed poorly.

Quests are boring and repetitive. They mostly involving a few rounds of going to a random location to fight some enemies, open a box, talk to an npc or even just stare at some guy for a whole minute. Sometimes there's extra requirements for not killing or being seen which mostly just do nothing or function as a random chance to fail the quest. The rewards for completing quests are some cash and skill points which are vital for progression, though you get very little per completion resulting in alot of tedious grinding.

Weapons are unsatisfying to use and lack variety, making combat a bore. Most types function almost identically, and the variety of weapons within each type forms a scale between near awful and kinda good, heavily weighted toward awful. Progressing up said scale involves sifting through random parts from loot and shops in the hopes they have better stats. There's seemingly no way to reliable get better parts aside from elite enemies which may rarely spawn out in the open, or function as a final fight for slogging through also rare enemy HQ buildings, and even then it still might randomly generate with bad stats bad stats. Once you do get a decent weapon it becomes useless fairly quickly when you move to a higher level area and you're back to scrounging.

Game progression boils down to capturing enemy base tiles while doing repetitive quests and combat in a number go up system with nothing really changing as you move forward. The only exception being the main story which you progress through by defeating boss enemies which spawn at progressively higher levels, which are just giant versions or the basic goons that spawn everywhere. I haven't found the story to be very interesting and isn't even necessary for progression, it just makes a few new enemy types spawn that function similarly to most others.

Overall the game leans on procedural generation in an infinite world in the absence of engaging core gameplay, leading to an experience that is interesting for a while but ends up feeling more like a slog the more you really get into it.

5089 is a worthy offering. If you enjoy the game play loop associated with looter shooters (think Borderlands) and you don't mind the primitive looking graphics (think Virtua Fighter), go ahead and scoop this one up. 

While it can be hard to get into at first, once you've run some quests, skilled up, and found a weapon that suits your play style it becomes a lot of fun.

Your character is highly customizable. Just keep dumping skill points where you want to improve and while you're earning more of those, combine parts for weapons and equipment as you find them. When you don't feel like you're improving, push out to a harder area. The world is procedurally generated and functionally endless so you can keep doing this for as look as you want.

There are some weak points that you may not enjoy, of course. The 3-D graphics are low poly and straight out of the early 90's. There's a tiny bit of a story in there but it isn't much and is finished quickly. If you're looking for cutting edge visuals and masterful storytelling, this isn't the game you're looking for.

If you're into solid game play, telling your own emergent story, and finding your own fun (do you have an imagination?), then this game is definitely worth it.

I had fun with 3089, but this version is a buggy mess (especially in coop) and the gameplay is starting to get really old and boring and the flaws are becoming too glaring to overlook.

Bugs: Enemies often skip all over rather than moving smoothly, making fast moving enemies impossible to hit. I'm playing over LAN and even with that my coop partner also appears to jump around unsmoothly. Quests become unfinishable and unfixable (its so bad they added a way to report unreachable objectives, but even THAT doesn't fix the issue sometimes). Enemies appear inside geometry and are unkillable, making it impossible to convert an area or finish certain quests. You can get stuck inside geometry, such as when taking down a stronghold. In co-op, enemies sometimes "clone", where it looks like you are damaging an enemy but when you destroy it, it shows an animation of the enemy being destroyed but the enemy remains standing back at full health. Just check the bug forum, there's endless bugs.

Combat is hideously boring. The core issue stems from the shooting - shots have travel time AND random bullet deviation. Why someone thought this was a fun thing to do in an FPS is beyond me.

So, it's an FPS, but aiming isn't a thing, the vast majority of weapons you find have abysmal accuracy, if you are lucky enough to find a weapon with high accuracy in a little bit it'll become obsolete and you'll have to hunt for another or accept awful boring "roll the dice" shooting. If you move to avoid enemy shots your accuracy gets even worse, so you may as well just stand still and tank the shots while shooting at the enemy and praying the bullet goes where you want. 

For some reason I was fine with this in the previous versions of the game but it's just gotten so tedious and boring. What is even the point of giving shots travel time if you are so heavily punished by moving and there's so much random deviation?

I finally rage quit after I needed to upgrade my weapon and after 30 minutes didn't find any with decent accuracy. I absolutely hate using the low accuracy weapons. It's an FPS for christsakes, shooting is supposed to be responsive and fun and satisfying, random bullet deviation should NOT be this extreme.

Armor / chips are seemingly pointless. You can get an entire piece of gear's worth of stats just from completing one quest. You'll waste more time trying to find better armor than you would just doing a quest.

Combat is feast or famine. Either you are OP and enemies go down in a few shots or you are too weak and each individual enemy is a slog to take down via repetitive, totally thought-free combat. Either way combat is just a boring, unpleasant grind.

Going through inventory is painful, there's no "compare" feature making it really annoying to try to compare 2 weapons. For a game that's all about upgrading gear it's inexcusable.

There is a really obnoxious type of enemy called a "floater" which can oneshot you even when you have so much armor that normal enemies hardly damage you. It suffers from the "jumpy" movement issue making it difficult to hit and it's a small sphere making it already hard to hit. It moves really fast, too, so you have to run away, turn and shoot it, run away further, and repeat until it teleports away and you have to go find it again. Combined with the awful accuracy of most weapons it's THE WORST.

VR is abysmal, the game just does NOT work in VR. It's an afterthought.

In short, it's a glitchy "FPS" game which fails to get the fundamental FPS gameplay right.

EDIT: Found out MANY others have complained about the gunplay being no fun, but the dev INSISTS that they are "satisfied" with the current state of gunplay. So no hope of this ever being fixed.

I played this game for 21 hours before writing a review, and I don't plan to finish it. Spoiler alert, it gets a positive review, but there's good news and bad news:

The good news is that this game delivers on its name. It's an action rpg.

The bad news is that it's an action rpg. That means that it takes the now standard formula of kill/fetch/give/protect quests from role-playing games, and embeds it into a 1st person shooter, complete with boss levels.

Like most computer rpgs out there, you grind for experience, which allows you to go to areas with more dangerous monsters, and bigger rewards. After defeating each boss, it unlocks another paragraph of the story.

Rinse and repeat.

It works flawlessly, but for me, the grind isn't worth the story. If the game was shorter, I would have nothing but praise, but the action isn't all that exciting, and the story moves too slowly to be worth the grind. Again, if this was a short game, I would have been satisfied, but now it feels like work.

I'll keep an eye out for Phr00t's work, because this is flawlessly executed for what it is, but Ive hit my grinding threshold with this one.

O jogo é único em todos os seus aspectos.
Possui uma história, atmosfera, jogabilidade e mecânica jamais vistas antes, sendo assim completamente inovador em comparação aos demais jogos do mercado.

Por mais que seja meio simples em aspectos gráficos (o que é intencional; uma vez que os gráficos condizem com a aurora do jogo) ele tem uma mecânica RPG realmente interessante, possibilitando escolher e criar sua própria classe, como também criar seus próprios equipamentos (como armaduras, armas, chips, tudo feito por você) mas também pode comprar todos esses equipamentos que NUNCA SÃO ÚNICOS, pois todos os equipamentos nas lojas do jogo são gerados aleatóriamente (cada peça é gerada de forma aleatória) o que faz o jogo sempre inovador em sua jogabilidade, já que cada item é diferente dos demais.

A jogabilidade é recheada de liberdade e escolhas para o jogador.
Tu além de poder até mesmo criar sua classe (ou escolher uma) existem várias formas em que tu pode jogar o jogo, cada uma tem seu modo único de se jogar. 
Tanta liberdade até que te possibilita escolher sua quest desejada em uma estação.
Pode escolher também qual região você deverá atacar e anexar à sua facção.
Você só segue o modo história do jogo quando bem entender e se sentir preparado.
Você usa o equipamento que bem entender (que pode ser customizado por você). Cada equipamento é melhor usado dependo de sua classe (novamente; que pode ser customizada por você).

Ele de certa forma nunca acaba. Tem uma história por trás dele, e tu pode seguir e tentar entender o contexto por trás do planeta XaX fazendo quests e matando bosses.
Porém mesmo seguindo esse rumo, o jogo nunca vai acabar pois tu tem a liberdade de continuar atacando e anexando regiões inimigas, o que acabam sendo meio que ''quests'' secundárias.
Logo seu save nunca acaba e demorá pra enjoar.

A aurora e atmosfera condizem perfeitamente ao contexto da história do jogo.
Realmente interessante essa cultura de '' ácido '' que o jogo apresenta dentro do Planeta XaX que está afundado em mistérios e uma guerra milênar.
Os gráficos e trilha sonora auxiliam nesse '' Estado de Espiríto '' que o jogador pode se conectar.

O jogo é muito bom, sendo único e inovador em todos seus aspectos.
Oferece grande nível de liberdade ao jogador, à tal ponto de customizar aspectos internos do jogo.
Ele dificilmente enjoa, uma vez que tudo nele é gerado aleatóriamente, como equipamentos, mapas, bases, personagens, etc...

When I came across this game in the steam store I instantly thought I must have it but not because it looked like a good game. In fact I thought id probably play for a small amount of time, joke around about it, and refund it before it was too late. However once I started playing I quickly became fascinated and couldnt seem to pull myself away from this game. Its quirkiness turns out to be awesome in fact I can say it is extremely fun to play. I cant help but imagine what playing this game would be like on acid. Amazing. In short, buy it.

So far the game has been a blast and overall I'd give it a 4.0 out of 5.0 in terms of playability. This isn't one of those games where an immersive story is going to make you forget reality, however the fast-paced gameplay certainly will have you forgetting about the world around you.

Random loot system makes for a great core game concept, particular in that your bot drops pieces of his gear if he should he be destroyed. Fall in love with a special sword or blaster? Don't, only your salty tears will be left behind.

I would like to see passive generation be upped, particularly concerning energy. I get the benefit of energy weapons is their ammo is infinite so long as you have energy remaining, however once you're near the 25% mark your life is likely going to follow suit awfully quickly as your enemies begin wailing as you await a recharge.
